explanation:
Bar magnets lose strength over time due to self-demagnetization, which occurs when the magnetic field lines from the north pole of one magnet attempt to enter the south pole of the other, creating a demagnetizing field. To prevent this, the magnets are stored with their unlike poles facing each other (North facing South). This arrangement allows the magnetic field lines to form a continuous, closed loop through the space between the magnets, minimizing the internal demagnetizing field. Additionally, soft iron keepers are placed at the outer ends of the magnets to provide a low-reluctance path for the remaining magnetic flux, further stabilizing the magnetic domains and preserving the magnets' strength.
